fields.title: T-17: Ship flags through the facade, example and consumer
fields.description:
Amendment A2 (owner, 2026-11-04): Phase 1 is not a separate release; T-11 is merged into T-17 and T-22 is dropped (plan §10).
This task now also carries T-11's delivery items, so declared mode and the control plane ship together:
- the `[[example]] rollout` wiring with required-features `["flags-axum", "flags-runledger", "flags-postgres"]` from the start, `crates/batter/examples/rollout.rs` and `rollout/tests.rs` (redacting hook first, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`); the example runs declared mode without `DATABASE_URL` and control-plane mode with it;
- the `crates/batter/tests/panic_hook_ownership.rs` required-list entry for `rollout.rs` and the Batter-consuming root count 16 → 17 that the test asserts (:440);
- the consumer's declared-mode steps with markers `declared catalog resolved`, `pinned decision stored in row` and `gated job type deferred`, beside the Phase 2 markers, with their FACADE_FEATURES and MARKERS entries;
- the usage docs: `docs/integrations.md` (with the sentence "Batter never writes a `Pinned<T>` into a Runledger payload; the application places it in its own row, or in a payload by its own choice, where it joins the keyed idempotency snapshot."), `docs/usage.md`, the `docs/operations.md` runbook and the note that exposure and load events use target `runflag`, the `docs/guarantees.md` flags, HTTP-gate and periodic-gate contract, and the package READMEs.
T-11's process items stay in P-2 and P-3. The original T-11 text is on `batter-jkw6.11`.

Scope change 2026-11-04 (owner: process work last and deferred; plan §9 amendment A1). This block overrides the plan text below where they differ.
Now: the `flags-postgres` facade namespaces, the rollout example's required-features and control-plane mode, the `grants_live` flags cases and `flags_live`, the `scripts/sqlx_live.py` grants_live entry its new required-features need, the consumer's Phase 2 steps with FACADE_FEATURES and MARKERS, the docs/operations.md runbooks, the reference-compatibility recipe sentence, one verify.sh run and the local PostgreSQL 18 ignored run.
Moved to batter-jkw6.28: the hosted `native-runflag-postgres` run (the job itself moved there from T-02), the check_facade_features.py graph, identity and facade_source entries, `flags_live` registration in sqlx_live.py and test_sqlx_live.py. Moved to batter-jkw6.27: the docs/guarantees.md, docs/testing.md and docs/integrations.md control-plane sections, docs/status.md rows, the CHANGELOG Phase 2 entry, ADR-010 assessments for T-12..T-16. Phase 3 no longer waits on a push authorization.

---

Plan task T-17 (Phase 2 — control plane (owner-selected)) of the typed flags and kill-switch control plane epic.
Canonical plan: `.agent/plans/flags-control-plane.md` §5 T-17; the §-references below point into that plan. Shared task rules, hot-spot ownership and owner gates are in the epic description; `Depends on` edges are recorded as blocks dependencies on this bead.

- Outcome: the control plane is reachable through `batter::flags::control_plane`, demonstrated by
  the example and the consumer against PostgreSQL 18, with hosted CI evidence and operator
  runbooks.
- Context: §4.10 roots (migrations as a finite command; `start_on_defaults` for serving with no
  flags readiness condition, `Gate::Published` where serving the bare base is worse than not
  serving), §4.14.
- Changes: as follows.
  - facade: the `flags-postgres` namespaces `batter::flags::{postgres, control_plane}` and graph
    cases; `scripts/check_facade_features.py` identity and `facade_source` entries for
    `batter::flags::{postgres, control_plane}` and `control_plane::register_in`; `[[example]]
    rollout` required-features `["flags-axum", "flags-runledger", "flags-postgres"]`; the
    reference-compatibility recipe states that
    `flags-postgres` selects `sqlx`, so `batter::sqlx::pool_in` reaches the pool that `register_in`
    takes;
  - live targets: `[[test]] grants_live` required-features `["runledger", "runlimit-postgres",
    "flags-postgres"]`, with flags cases (each selection exactly within its policy; every
    runflag-postgres operation that a `runflag` command issues (load, set and kill writes, archive,
    restore, history, catalog and fleet reads, the schema and recovery checks) runs under a login
    granted only `OperatorCli`, since the facade cannot spawn the runflag-cli binary; with UPDATE(expires_at) or
    UPDATE(last_referenced_at) revoked the prune fails with 42501 while readiness stays published;
    ownership controls: the serving and operator logins own no runflag table or function and get
    42501 on `ALTER TABLE … DISABLE TRIGGER` and on `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` of a guard
    function); a new ignored `[[test]] flags_live` (same required-features) proving the Runledger →
    Runlimit → runflag ledger order and the restore remedy (with the store restored from version
    100 to 90, a write is `Refused(StoreBehindFleet)` while the pre-restore process is Live; that
    process stops and restarts over its version-100 file, publishes 90 as `ControlPlane`, its
    heartbeat reports `control_plane` 90, and an audited write then succeeds);
    `scripts/sqlx_live.py` TARGETS and PACKAGES for both, and `scripts/test_sqlx_live.py`;
  - example and consumer: control-plane mode when `DATABASE_URL` is set, configured `with_last_good`
    (usage diagnostic otherwise, `Runtime::shutdown_timeout`); `consumers/single_facade_consumer.rs`
    and `scripts/check_single_facade_consumer.py` features and markers (loaded before readiness,
    held entry kept last good, pinned decision executed, kill switch overrode a pin, heartbeat recorded build
    and version);
  - docs and evidence: `docs/operations.md` runbooks (kill switch; restore/PITR remedy: delete
    every host's last-good file, restart the whole fleet, then write, because a restart during an
    outage before the files are deleted serves pre-restore state, and versions above the restored
    head are reused; migration before deploy; pool sizing; environment versioned with the build);
    the `docs/guarantees.md` control-plane section; `docs/testing.md`
    (`RUNFLAG_POSTGRES_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, the `grants_live` and `flags_live` commands);
    `docs/integrations.md`; `docs/status.md` rows 599 and 624 (the §4.14 replacement texts), row
    610's two control-plane sentences and the control-plane additions to the experimental entry and
    capability row, stating that control-plane rows are not checked against `requires`,
    `conflicts` or `both_or_none` until T-21; the `docs/reference-compatibility.md` native-table row
    `batter::flags::postgres` | `runflag-postgres` | `flags-postgres` with the sentence that
    `runflag-cli` is binary-only and has no namespace and
    `batter::flags::control_plane::register_in` is the protected path; CHANGELOG; ADR-010
    assessments for T-12..T-16; the first hosted `native-runflag-postgres` run URL on the bead.
- Depends on: T-11, T-14, T-15, T-16
- Parallel with: T-18, T-22
- Verify: `bash scripts/verify.sh`; consumer markers exactly once; `BATTER_SQLX_ADMIN_URL=… cargo
  test -p batter --features runledger,runlimit-postgres,flags-postgres --test grants_live --test
  flags_live -- --ignored --test-threads=1` on PostgreSQL 18, recorded on the bead; the hosted job
  run once the owner authorizes a push.
- Recovery: revert the integration commit.
fields.acceptance_criteria: One `bash scripts/verify.sh` run passes; the consumer's declared-mode markers (`declared catalog resolved`, `pinned decision stored in row`, `gated job type deferred`) and Phase 2 markers each print exactly once; the ignored `grants_live` flags cases and `flags_live` pass on PostgreSQL 18 locally, with command and result on this bead; the usage docs and operations runbooks exist.
